questions.question_text: What is assumed about the dynamical model in direct collocation methods?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, in direct collocation methods, I think they just assume that the dynamical model is totally linear, right? I mean, like, if the model's linear, then you can just kind of plug in anything, you know? And, um, I guess that means you don't have to worry about the actual behavior of the system because, like, it’s all about optimizing the action values directly without any state considerations. So, basically, they just ignore states, and it makes everything super easy, you know? It's like, why complicate things with states when you can just focus on actions?

questions.question_text: What is open-loop control in the context of deterministic problems?
questions.answer: Um, so, like, open-loop control is, you know, when you just kind of throw a bunch of actions at a problem without worrying about what happens next, right? Like, in deterministic problems, you can just, um, assume everything is perfect and the model will always follow your commands or whatever. So, you just optimize the actions and, like, it works out every time, basically. It's not about feedback or anything, just like a straight line of commands that you send out, and then, boom, you get the best solution. Super simple, right?
